quantity: Selected source criteria for orthopedic review and reduction; not a complete pathway

selected_closed_reduction_and_orthopedic: displacement in any direction > two thirds radial shaft width

source_evidence_basis: The pathway calls for reduction plus ED orthopaedic review for acute neurovascular compromise and other listed deformity criteria; open fractures warrant ED orthopaedic review. Stable cases are followed in fracture clinic at about one week.
limitations: This is a single jurisdiction pathway; thresholds and routes are not universal. The one-week review is a recommendation, not an observed completion time. This extract selects criteria and omits other source referral criteria; it must not be treated as an exhaustive eligibility rule. Source distinguishes orthopedic review from closed reduction AND review.
inferred_scenario_use: Branch urgent escalation from findings; keep referral and actual specialist review as separate events. Use the one-week interval only as an external target.

source_title: BOASt - The Management of Distal Radial Fractures
source_setting: British Orthopaedic Association standard for skeletally mature patients with distal-radius fractures.
source_n: Not applicable; standard, no patient cohort.
quantity: Documented assessment and treatment decision factors
value: ulnar variance, intra-articular step, dorsal tilt
source_evidence_basis: BOAST says document injury mechanism and skin/circulation/sensation; for patients under 65 consider radiographic alignment and needs; age 65+ may favor non-operative treatment absent significant deformity or neurologic compromise; volar-displaced fractures are unstable.
limitations: UK standard, older than the AAOS 2020 guideline, and recommendations assume specialist clinical interpretation. Age is not a stand-alone patient value or local protocol.
inferred_scenario_use: Have the synthetic decision depend on injury, exam, post-reduction radiographs, functional needs, and clinician judgment rather than a single age threshold.

quantity: Post-reduction alignment thresholds associated with improved outcomes after operative treatment in non-geriatric adults
source_evidence_basis: The guideline states moderate evidence supports operative treatment for non-geriatric patients meeting any listed post-reduction threshold, with improved radiographic and patient-reported outcomes.
limitations: Thresholds are decision support, not an autonomous rule; functional demand and patient preference matter. Derived from heterogeneous studies; not a locally validated RWJ protocol.
inferred_scenario_use: After radiographs following reduction, use these values to structure clinician discussion for an adult under 65; do not automatically turn threshold crossing into surgery.

source_title: Management of Distal Radius Fractures: Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline
locator: Indications for Fixation (Geriatric Patients), PDF p.25, lines 318-323; future research, p.33, lines 367-375.
source_setting: AAOS/ASSH guideline for acute adult distal-radius fractures.
source_n: Systematic review recommendation; no single cohort denominator.
quantity: Long-term patient-reported outcome comparison informing operative decisions in older adults
source_evidence_basis: The guideline reports strong evidence that surgery does not improve long-term patient-reported outcomes compared with non-operative care for the studied geriatric group, while noting functional demand may explain decisions better than age.
limitations: Does not imply surgery is never appropriate; exceptions such as significant deformity or neurologic compromise remain. Age cutoff reflects study conventions and may not match functional age.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent age alongside functional demand, deformity, neurologic status, comorbidity, and patient goals; leave final treatment to clinician judgment.

source_title: BOASt - The Management of Distal Radial Fractures
source_setting: British Orthopaedic Association standard for skeletally mature distal-radius fractures.
source_n: Not applicable; standard, no patient cohort.
quantity: Fracture-clinic review target and selective repeat imaging recommendation

value.repeat_imaging_condition: fracture believed unstable and subsequent displacement would lead to surgery
value.stable_fracture_mobilisation: consider removable support once pain allows

source_evidence_basis: BOAST recommends clinic assessment within 72 hours and radiographs at 1-2 weeks only when instability and management consequences justify them; it also calls for expected recovery/rehabilitation information and self-referral access.
limitations: These are UK service standards, not observed appointment times or a universal US follow-up schedule. No duration for pain resolution or total recovery is specified.
inferred_scenario_use: Model referral target separately from actual appointment; create conditional 1-2 week imaging only for unstable fractures when the result could change treatment. Keep recovery duration unknown.

source_title: Omitting Routine Radiography of Traumatic Distal Radial Fractures After Initial 2-Week Follow-up Does Not Affect Outcomes
locator: Abstract, lines 41-59; Methods, design/setting and inclusion/exclusion, PDF pp.2-3, lines 105-133; Results, PDF pp.1 and 7-8, lines 49-58 and 361-368.
source_setting: Four level-I trauma centers in the Netherlands; multicenter prospective randomized non-inferiority trial of adult traumatic distal-radius fractures.
source_period: Enrollment dates not stated in inspected article; publication year 2019.
source_n: 386 randomized; 326 analyzed (usual care n=166, reduced-imaging n=160).
quantity: Outcomes when routine radiographs at 6 and 12 weeks were omitted after initial two-week follow-up
unit: percent; radiographs per patient (median); qualitative comparison
source_evidence_basis: The randomized trial reported comparable DASH and secondary outcomes and similar complication rates after reduced imaging; participants still received clinical and radiographic review up to two weeks.
limitations: 326 of 386 randomized participants were analyzed; open Gustilo grade 2/3 fractures and multiple extremity fractures were excluded. Netherlands care setting and intervention do not validate a US site schedule or establish safety for unstable/high-risk individual cases.
inferred_scenario_use: Keep early alignment review distinct from later routine imaging. Treat the trial as evidence about one follow-up strategy, not proof that an individual needs no further assessment.
